thread:
incidents-bot: Paging: SLO p99 spike observed on streaming responses (EU region). Auto-triggered page to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Please ack. :rotating_light:

lina: acked. seeing p95 ~420ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~5.2s for SSE endpoints. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/streams?query=eu.sse.latency

ben: on it. any customer reports?

sasha: customer-success: one customer (FinCard) just filed a support ticket about stalled chat responses. They report 10s+ stalls intermittently. Ticket ID: CS-8812.

ravi: initial thought: proxy layer (edge-proxy v2.3.1) had increased write queue depth. hitting write buffer limits -> chunking delayed. checking proxy logs now.

jade: I'm running `kubectl logs -n runtime edge-proxy-7f8d` filtered for writeback errors. seeing `E write: timeout after 8s` repeated. Also many connections show `slow consumer` events.

ben: any rollout or deploys in last hour?

lina: No deploys to runtime in EU in last 90m. There was an autoscale event ~30m ago.

ops-bot: ALERT: autoscaler triggered +20 pods at 2026-03-15T11:10:03Z for runtime-eu.

ravi: autoscale could have temporarily changed LB distribution, causing client fanout shift. but write timeouts indicate backpressure from downstream consumer sockets (client slow reads). need to see client ack windowing behavior.

ben: can we verify whether KV cache or batching caused large frames? Any sudden increase in chunk size?

jade: pulling sample chunk sizes from the edge-proxy metrics: 99th chunk size increased from 4KB -> 28KB around 11:07. suspicious.

lina: also p99 tokens/sec per connection spiked for a subset of flows (long-running chats). looks like single-client read stalls accumulating and blocking server write loop.

ravi: mitigation idea: enable aggressive keepalive + smaller write buffers at proxy to prevent head-of-line blocking. We can flip a config flag `edge.write_batch_max_bytes=8192` and reduce `connection.write_timeout=3s`.

ben: agree. want a quick canary change on one AZ. lina can you coordinate?

lina: prepping canary. will patch config on proxy pool eu-west-1a edge-proxy-asg-1. Doing live patch using conf-agent: `conf-agent apply --service edge-proxy --env eu-west-1a --set edge.write_batch_max_bytes=8192,connection.write_timeout=3s`

jade: preflight check: health checks will remain active. Rolling config patch should not restart pods.

(5m pass)

lina: canary applied to eu-west-1a. Observability: latency p99 on that AZ dropped from 5.2s -> 700ms within 90s.

ben: good sign. monitoring other AZs while we rollout.

ravi: initiating rollout to remaining EU proxies with 20s stagger.

(rollout proceeds)

sasha: customer-success: informed FinCard that we are investigating and applied mitigations in EU; asked for confirmation if they still see stalls.

(10m later)

ben: overall p99 across EU down to 820ms, p95 ~360ms. number of `write: timeout` errors decreased 95%.

jade: logs show fewer `slow consumer` events. also see fewer large chunk emissions; batch size histograms tightened.

ravi: root cause hypothesis: a combination of (1) autoscaler rebalancing opened new connections and caused some clients to slow-read (mobile clients on flaky networks), (2) proxy default batching allowed large write coalescing that blocked the vertex write loop when a single slow connection stalled, (3) keepalive timers at 8s delayed detection of stuck sockets.

lina: impact summary: transient p95/p99 SLO breach for ~18m, specific to streaming SSE/WebSocket endpoints in EU region, affecting ~0.7% of active streams and 1 enterprise customer (FinCard) with noticeable stalls. No data loss, no request failures beyond timeouts on extremely slow connections.

sasha: CS update sent: FinCard acknowledged and will monitor. offered to escalate to SOC if they see further degradation.

ben: next steps:
- full rollout config change to all EU proxies (done)
- create a follow-up PR to make conservative defaults for write batching and keepalive for streaming endpoints
- instrument per-connection read-rate and connection-age to detect slow-consumer patterns early
- add a circuit to drop oversized coalesced writes when a connection is diagnosed slow (graceful degrade)

ravi: i'll own the PR for proxy defaults and the config flags. target: tomorrow EOD.

jade: I'll open an ops runbook entry for this pattern ("streaming slow-consumer head-of-line blocking") with playbook steps and runbook links.

lina: handoff to night on-call: @jade you are taking over. please monitor EU p99 and CS escalations.

jade: acked, taking over. set pager to watch: `alerts/streams.europe.p99 > 1.5s for 5m` and the incident channel for CS pings.

incidents-bot: Incident auto-close candidate: no active errors for 30m. Please confirm before manual close.

lina: marking for postmortem. I'll collect traces and sidecar histograms and add to PM doc.

sasha: adding customer notes and timeline to CS ticket CS-8812.

ben: thanks all. good mitigation. tagging for postmortem: eng-runtime, eng-sre, eng-platform, customer-success.

jade: closing watch but will reopen if alerts recur. :white_check_mark:
